newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Friday with a falling domestic A share market in Shanghai pushing funds back to the repo market, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day fell to 11.51 percent from 12.00 percent on Thursday.

Turnover plunged to 5.12 million lots from 12.91 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills. Shanghai's A share index closed down 0.89 percent on Friday. Two new companies, Tibet Jinzhu and WuHan Hanshang Group were listed on the bourse today.

"The A share market fall disheartened investors," said one trader. "The seven-day contract lost ground despite the new listings, indicating investors were reluctant to borrow funds on the repo market for share speculation."
Traders believe the A market performance will continue to be a key factor early next week.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Friday on a technical rebound after successive falls in the past few weeks, traders said.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose to 1.10 million lots from 886,566 lots.
The three-year bond that matures in August 1999 became the most active contract today, ending up at 103.57 yuan from 103.51 yuan.
"The spot market made a technical recovery today after a long-term consolidation," one trader said. "But the poor market fundamentals have not changed."
